intro: Every what has a why: a tariff, a fee or a delayed parcel is the last link of a chain that starts with a conflict, a rivalry or an election. Each storyline follows one chain from geopolitics through decisions and market reactions to the parcel, so you can see what moves cost, speed, volume, compliance and networks, and what comes next.

storylines.title: The end of duty-free parcels
storylines.why: Washington, Brussels, London and Tokyo have decided that duty-free entry for low-value parcels became a subsidy to foreign sellers, a revenue leak and a blind spot for safety and security checks. Each is closing it on its own timetable and with its own data rules, while Brazil, heading into an election, went the other way.

geopolitics.text: Beijing asked the EU for a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese companies as Brussels prepared its parcel fee.
In Brazil a poll found 62% naming the small-parcel tax the government's biggest mistake, ahead of the October election.
China's trade surplus with the EU reached €360.6 billion in 2025, and Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič called the trend not sustainable.

decision.text: The United States suspended its $800 de minimis exemption indefinitely for all modes, from 24 June for express and 24 July for mail, with a statutory repeal from 1 July 2027.
The EU charges a flat €3 customs duty per tariff category on parcels up to €150, as an interim measure until 1 July 2028.
The UK confirmed it will remove its £135 low-value customs relief by October 2028 and make sellers and marketplaces liable for the duty.
Japan's 2026 tax reform ends the consumption tax exemption for imports of ¥10,000 or less, with foreign sellers and large platforms collecting at the point of sale.
Brazil signed into law a zero federal import tax on purchases up to $50 through certified platforms, while the state ICMS tax still applies.

market.text: After the American exemption ended for all origins, 88 postal operators suspended some or all US-bound services and US-bound mail from UPU members fell 81% in a week.
Liège Airport reported e-commerce parcels down 24% in July, and French customs put the fall in Chinese parcel imports at 30% to 40% since the EU duty started.
Temu's owner is investing in local fulfilment, and Amazon says 97% of its EU shipments already leave from European warehouses.
Brazil went the other way: import declarations rose 74% year on year in August after the zero rate.

parcel.text: Every consignment becomes a customs declaration: the new US postal informal entry needs a 10-digit classification, origin, value and an eligible filer for each item.
Flat charges weigh most on cheap goods: on a €6 accessory, the EU's €3 duty and €2 fee almost double the price.
Direct China to consumer air parcels into the US and the EU have fallen to a structurally lower level, Brazil being the exception.
Fast-moving items move into bonded and domestic warehouses, so value shifts from long-haul air lanes to import clearance and destination fulfilment.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: outside Brazil, the duty-free direct parcel is in structural, not cyclical, decline, and the remaining flow pays per declaration rather than per kilo. The next contest is over who files and on what data, which favours operators with delivered duty paid capability and clean item-level customs data.

next.text: United States: compliance date for partner agency requirements under the postal informal entry rule
EU: €2 handling fee per item on low-value distance sales becomes chargeable
United States: statutory repeal of the de minimis exemption takes effect
Japan: consumption tax collected at the point of sale on imports of ¥10,000 or less

storylines.title: Europe rewrites customs
storylines.why: Brussels concluded that a customs system built for containers could not police billions of small parcels, most of them from China, that entered duty-free and often failed safety checks. Its answer is to charge every parcel and make the platform, not the shopper, the accountable importer, backed by a new agency and a single data hub.

geopolitics.text: Member states split: France and Romania imposed national parcel charges, while the Netherlands and Belgium dropped theirs for fear of traffic moving to neighbouring gateways.
China's €360.6 billion trade surplus with the EU in 2025 hardened the Commission's line, with Maroš Šefčovič calling the trend not sustainable.
After the Commission's €550 million fine on AliExpress, Beijing said it firmly opposes digital barriers imposed under the pretext of platform regulation.

decision.text: Romania has charged 25 lei, about €5, per non-EU parcel under €150 since 1 January.
A flat €3 customs duty applies per tariff subheading in low-value e-commerce consignments, until 1 July 2028.

The reformed customs code entered into force, making platforms and non-EU sellers the importer for distance sales, with fines of 1% to 6% of annual import value and importer obligations applying from 21 September 2027.
The Commission set the Union handling fee at €2 per item from 1 November, subject to a 30-day objection period; KPMG reads the unit as per product category.
Italy's own €2 contribution per consignment, postponed several times, is now due from 1 December.
The EU Customs Data Hub, run by the new EU Customs Authority in Lille from 2027, becomes mandatory for e-commerce operators.

market.text: After France's national tax started, small-parcel declarations at Paris-Charles de Gaulle fell 92%, largely as flows moved to other entry points.
Chinese air e-commerce exports to Europe were down 40% year on year in August, and inbound capacity fell 58% at Budapest and 35% at Liège.
Belgian customs counted 53% fewer small parcels and Dutch customs 46% fewer e-commerce parcels than a year earlier.
PostNL's international parcels fell about 15% in the first half, citing new EU import duties, and CTT's customs clearance business was hit.

parcel.text: A €10 basket with one tariff line carries €3 of duty and, from November, €2 of handling fee: a 50% uplift before VAT.
The importer of record shifts to platforms and sellers, with fines of up to 6% of a year's import value for repeated breaches.
Low-value parcels into Belgium and the Netherlands, which handle almost half of EU low-value imports, have roughly halved.
Integrators have warned that unworkable data rules risk shipments being held at EU borders, slowing transit at peak.
A charge in one country moves parcels to another gateway within days, so gateway choice turns on clearance speed and data capability.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: from 1 November the cheapest parcel into the EU carries at least €5 of charges before VAT, so the direct channel shrinks to a long tail while bulk imports into EU warehouses grow. The real dispute is over who holds importer liability and the customs data, and it will be settled in platform contracts before 21 September 2027.

next.text: EU €2 handling fee per item becomes chargeable on distance sales under €150
Italy's national €2 contribution per low-value consignment due to start
General application of the reformed customs code, including importer obligations and penalties
EU Customs Data Hub mandatory for e-commerce; the €3 flat duty expires

storylines.title: Hormuz and the fuel bill
storylines.why: The war between the United States and Iran that began on 28 February has turned the Strait of Hormuz into a permit regime and kept Brent above $100. The parcel pays through jet fuel, surcharges, war-risk premiums and longer detours around the Gulf gateways.

geopolitics.text: United States and Israeli strikes on Iran started the war, and the Revolutionary Guard closed the strait to most foreign shipping within days.
The June memorandum that ended active fighting collapsed in mid-July, when Iran declared it no longer valid and new strikes followed near the strait.
Yemen's Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, threatening the Red Sea outlet Riyadh uses to bypass Hormuz.
President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the strait, and Brent rose above $107 on 28 September.

decision.text: Saudi Arabia's ports authority launched logistics corridors to reroute Gulf cargo to Red Sea ports, with rail and truck links onward.
The United States Postal Service applies an 8% temporary fuel surcharge on parcel products until 17 January 2027.
Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority requires prior authorisation for transits and keeps a list of banned vessels.
Washington reimposed its naval blockade of Iranian ports and threatens sanctions on any entity that pays Iran for transit.
Dubai Customs raised its duty exemption for cross-border e-commerce shipments from 300 to 1,000 dirhams to cut costs for the sector.

market.text: FedEx and UPS added Middle East surcharges and raised fuel surcharge tables, with UPS's air import surcharge reaching 34.5%.
FedEx reported quarterly fuel expense up 66% year on year to $1.43 billion.
Jebel Ali handled 374,000 TEU in the second quarter, a 90% fall, and DP World's profit attributable to owners fell 47.3% in the first half.
Aramex posted record quarterly revenue, up 22%, selling alternative routes including land solutions and charters.
Jet fuel prices were up 116.5% year on year on 18 September, according to Baltic Exchange data.

parcel.text: Fuel surcharges pass through mechanically: the average net fuel surcharge per package rose 40% year on year in the second quarter.
Gulf deliveries are slower: sea transit from China to the Middle East stretched to 35 to 45 days and Temu delivery estimates to 20 days.
Gulf-bound cargo detours via Khor Fakkan, Fujairah, Salalah and Saudi Red Sea ports at four to five times the cost of sailing to Jebel Ali.
In August, Middle East to Asia air cargo volumes fell 11.0% and Europe to Middle East 12.1% year on year.
Any fee paid to Iran's strait authority can expose carriers and customers to United States sanctions, so Gulf routings need sanctions screening.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: neither Washington nor Tehran yet sees a cost high enough to move first, so a managed disruption into 2027 is likelier than a quick reopening. Fuel and conflict surcharges will outlast any ceasefire because insurers and refiners reprice with a lag, so parcel contracts should separate them from base rates.

next.text: Last of four Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd Gemini services sails via the Red Sea and Suez
United States midterm elections
End of the USPS temporary 8% fuel surcharge on parcel products

storylines.title: US and China, tariffs and truces
storylines.why: Washington uses access to its market as leverage over Beijing, and Beijing answers with its control of rare earths; neither wants a rupture, so they trade short truces. When the Supreme Court removed the emergency tariff tool, Washington rebuilt its tariffs on other statutes, but the duty-free parcel did not come back.

geopolitics.text: The Supreme Court struck down the tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.
A bilateral Board of Trade was set up during President Trump's visit to Beijing to negotiate tariff lists.
During Xi Jinping's state visit the truce was extended to 10 January 2027, with China keeping its pause on new rare-earth export controls.
China asked for easier access to advanced artificial intelligence chips at the September summit and did not get it.

decision.text: USTR opened Section 301 investigations into structural excess capacity in 16 economies, with findings still pending.
CBP suspended the de minimis exemption for all modes, and nothing in the truce reopens duty-free entry for low-value shipments.
A 12.5% Section 301 tariff applies to Chinese products, part of a forced-labour action covering some 60 economies after the Section 122 surcharge lapsed.
The two sides agreed tariff cuts on about $60 billion of trade, $30 billion each way, returning about 90% of listed products to MFN rates; Washington has not published a start date.

market.text: UPS returned to year-on-year volume growth on the China to United States lane.
Chinese e-commerce air exports to North America were roughly flat in August while those to Europe fell 40%.
Northeast Asia to North America air rates held at $5.76 per kg while China to Western Europe fell to $3.85.
PDD's net income fell 12% in the second quarter as it onboards local merchants and invests in local warehousing.

parcel.text: China-origin parcels pay 12.5% under Section 301 on top of normal duties, and the truce does not change that for parcels.
Transpacific e-commerce volume has recovered while China to Europe falls, as capacity is redeployed to the Pacific.
The flow changes format: platforms ship in bulk to American warehouses and sell through local merchants, so the parcel arrives as a domestic shipment.
The Section 301 rates are tied to forced-labour import policy, so origin and supplier evidence now decide the rate a parcel pays.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: the truces are getting shorter and cover bulk trade in non-sensitive goods, not the parcel, so planning should assume no return of duty-free entry to the United States whatever happens at APEC. Each expiry date, now 10 January 2027, is a repricing date for transpacific capacity and for any contract priced on current tariffs.

next.text: United States midterm elections
APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, with Trump reported to attend
Expiry of the extended Washington-Beijing truce and the pause on rare-earth export controls

storylines.title: Chinese platforms move the warehouse
storylines.why: As Western governments tax every small parcel, China's platforms keep selling by changing format: they ship in containers, clear once and deliver from warehouses inside the market. Beijing finances the shift as export policy, so the volume stays but moves from air mail to domestic last mile.

geopolitics.text: China's 15th Five-Year Plan doubled down on self-reliance and domestic supply chains, with exports adapting through Chinese-controlled stock abroad.
Beijing said it firmly opposes the EU's digital barriers after the AliExpress fine, and promised support for Chinese firms abroad.

decision.text: A nine-ministry plan treats overseas warehouses as strategic infrastructure, with financing, export credit insurance and faster clearance.
A tax rule lets Chinese exporters claim rebates when goods leave for an overseas warehouse, before they are sold.
The Commission fined Temu €200 million under the Digital Services Act, followed by €550 million for AliExpress in July.
A draft amendment to China's E-Commerce Law extends oversight to logistics and payment providers and adds countermeasure provisions.
The EU customs reform gives lower handling fees to non-EU sellers that consolidate shipments through EU warehouses.

market.text: Cainiao announced robotic warehouses across seven markets and JD.com launched Joybuy in six European markets on a local-warehouse model.
Shein opened a 376,000 sq ft automated centre at Cannock in the UK, part of a €250 million European logistics plan.
China's exports through overseas warehouses grew 3.3-fold in the first half, according to customs.
Shein's sales fell 15% between June and July against 50% for Temu, a gap attributed to its warehouse in Poland.
AliExpress reached operating profit on logistics optimisation as Alibaba's international sourcing shifted towards local supply.

parcel.text: China's low-value and e-commerce exports to Europe fell 25% year on year in July.
A per-parcel duty punishes low order values, while the same goods shipped in bulk pay duty on declared value spread over thousands of units.
Warehouse demand in the Netherlands, Germany and Poland has pushed vacancy near 3% and rents up more than 35%.
Local stock lets platforms offer faster delivery, such as Joybuy's same-day model in Europe.
Carriers and warehouses handling Chinese platform volume may face data requests from both Brussels and Beijing.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: the direct-from-China parcel splits into a long tail that keeps flying and pays the fees, and best sellers that move into local stock and leave the cross-border statistics. Chinese logistics groups follow the volume abroad, so local posts and carriers will meet them as competitors in the last mile, not only as customers.

next.text: EU €2 handling fee per item becomes chargeable, with lower fees for consolidated imports into EU warehouses
Singles' Day peak in China
Expiry of the extended Washington-Beijing truce

storylines.title: North America's yearly leash
storylines.why: Washington treats access to its market as leverage over its neighbours, pushing Mexico and Canada to screen out Chinese content and give ground on cars, dairy and steel. Refusing to renew the USMCA and taxing Canadian goods under a 1930 statute keep both partners on a short, annual leash.

geopolitics.text: At the six-year joint review, Washington declined to renew the USMCA, which stays in force but now faces a review every year.
Cars are the main sticking point: the United States wants 82% regional content, including 50% American content, against 75% today.
A survey of registered voters found 75% saying tariffs will matter to their vote in the midterms.

decision.text: Mexico raised its simplified courier rate for goods from non-treaty countries from 19% to 33.5%.
Mexico added tariffs of 5% to 50% on goods from countries without a trade agreement, mainly China, with textiles and clothing at 25% to 35% and footwear at 25%.
A 10% Section 301 tariff applies to Canada and Mexico; law firms report USMCA-qualifying goods exempt, which the Federal Register summary does not state.
A 50% Section 338 duty applies to about $20 billion of Canadian goods across 554 tariff lines, with no USMCA exemption.
Canada answered with counter-tariffs on C$27.6 billion of American goods and a C$7.5 billion support package.

market.text: 542 fewer Canadian enterprises exported to the United States in 2025, the largest drop since 2020, concentrated among small firms.
A year after the 33.5% rate, Mexican logistics players describe a shift from direct air parcels to containers cleared and fulfilled locally.
The Canadian Federation of Independent Business says 18% of small exporters would not stay viable if tariffs last three months or more.

parcel.text: Canadian maple syrup, alcohol and hockey equipment sent to American buyers pay a 50% duty on top of clearance costs.
Postal shipments into the United States pay duty even when goods qualify under the trade agreement, while couriers can still claim the preference.
Fewer small Canadian firms ship to the United States, and Asian direct parcels into Mexico are giving way to containers.
In Mexico the growth business is fulfilment and domestic last mile, not cross-border parcels.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: an annual review turns every July into a renegotiation, so cross-border parcel contracts inside North America need change-of-law clauses rather than multi-year price commitments. Low-value relief inside the region is now one-way, which pushes Canadian and Mexican sellers towards stock held inside the United States.

next.text: United States midterm elections
Next annual USMCA joint review; statutory repeal of the US de minimis exemption

storylines.title: Latin America splits on the parcel
storylines.why: Across Latin America the cheap imported parcel is both a cost-of-living issue at the ballot box and an industrial-policy grievance. Brazil and Argentina have sided with the shopper, Mexico with the factory, and the next fight is over consumption taxes and the data platforms must hand over.

geopolitics.text: A poll found 62% of Brazilians naming the small-parcel tax the government's biggest mistake, ahead of the October election.
The EU-Mercosur agreement took provisional effect, while the European Parliament has referred it to the EU's top court.
Washington confirmed a 25% Section 301 tariff on Brazilian goods, citing practices including the Pix payment system.

decision.text: Chile charges 19% VAT through foreign platforms on goods up to $500.
Mexico's 33.5% courier rate for non-treaty origins was followed by tariffs of 5% to 50% on 1,463 tariff lines, mainly from China.
Argentina unified postal and courier treatment by decree and extended the $3,000 per-shipment cap to the postal channel.
Brazil's Law 15,502 confirms a zero federal import tax up to $50 via Remessa Conforme and adds seller-vetting and reporting duties for platforms; state ICMS of 17% to 20% still applies.
Brazil's new federal consumption tax, CBS, takes full effect, ahead of IBS gradually replacing ICMS from 2029.

market.text: Argentina's courier imports reached $518 million from January to May, up 113% year on year.
Brazil recorded 26.5 million import declarations in August, up 74% year on year.
Mercado Libre's items sold rose 45%, with cross-border GMV up 60% and volume through its China fulfilment centre up 170% on the quarter.
Correios lost R$5.6 billion in the first half; international parcels had fallen from about 22% of its revenue in 2024 to 8% in 2025.

parcel.text: Direct parcels into Brazil and Argentina are growing fast after the tax cuts and higher caps.
Brazil's zero federal rate makes a $50 basket cheaper but not untaxed, since state ICMS still applies.
Platforms must verify seller identity and bank data, monitor split shipments and report quarterly, so clearance data requirements tighten.
In Mexico, high parcel rates relocate Asian volume into containers, local fulfilment and domestic last mile.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: Brazil's zero rate is likely to hold through the election because both leading candidates back it, so the reversal risk moves to the 2027 consumption tax design, the Supreme Court case and the Finance Ministry reviews. Lanes into Brazil and Argentina are open but politically reversible, while Mexico rewards local stock over parcels.

next.text: Brazil general election, first round
Brazilian presidential run-off, if needed
CBS takes full effect in Brazil; watch how it applies to low-value imports

storylines.title: ASEAN's digital rulebook and China+1
storylines.why: Southeast Asia sits between Washington's hunt for Chinese goods routed through its factories and Beijing's push for deeper regional integration. ASEAN answers by hedging: one digital rulebook for the region, tighter national taxes on cheap parcels, and origin checks for American-bound flows.

geopolitics.text: China and ASEAN signed the Free Trade Area 3.0 upgrade protocol, adding chapters on the digital economy and supply chain connectivity.
A White House report on transshipment placed Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia in Tier 2 for rerouting risk; Beijing called it a false narrative.
India said it would finalise a trade deal with Washington only once it gets a preferential rate over Asian competitors.

decision.text: Thailand collects import duty on online purchases from 1 baht, affecting an estimated 250 million parcels a year.
ASEAN concluded negotiations on its Digital Economy Framework Agreement, with signature planned at the Manila summit on 16 to 18 November.
Indonesia's Permendag 19/2026 keeps a $100 FOB per-unit floor for cross-border goods and tightens seller vetting.
Section 301 tariffs add 10% on Indonesia, Malaysia and Cambodia and 12.5% on Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore and the Philippines.
Japan ends its ¥10,000 consumption-tax exemption, with platforms becoming deemed suppliers.

market.text: Thailand's customs department signed agreements with Lazada, Shopee, SHEIN, TikTok Shop and Temu to screen and collect upstream.
J&T handled 2.755 billion parcels in Southeast Asia in the second quarter, up 63.2%.
Shopee reported $38.3 billion of gross merchandise value in the second quarter, up 28.4%, on 4.2 billion orders.
China-ASEAN goods trade reached $744.41 billion from January to July, up 24.7% year on year.

parcel.text: Origin evidence at item level becomes the price of access to the American market for lanes from Tier 2 origins.
A hold on a consolidated shipment from a Tier 2 origin delays every parcel in it.
Direct parcels into Thailand now pay duty, at rates officials put around 30% for fashion and 20% for bags.
Intra-regional domestic parcel volume keeps compounding, led by platform-assigned carriers.
Every barrier on a cross-border parcel pushes stock into in-market fulfilment, favouring platform-owned logistics.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: DEFA will lower the cost of exchanging customs and payment data but will not unify Vietnamese VAT, Thai duties, Indonesian price floors or Japan's 2028 regime, so carriers face parallel compliance tracks. Value shifts to in-market stock and to operators that can prove origin item by item on American-bound lanes.

next.text: 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, planned signature of DEFA (16 to 18 November)
Japan opens registration for sellers of low-value goods
Japan ends the ¥10,000 consumption-tax exemption on low-value imports

storylines.title: North Africa as Europe's gateway
storylines.why: Europe wants supply chains closer to home and away from contested sea lanes, and Morocco sells itself as the industrial back office on its doorstep while Chinese investors use it as a base to serve European factories. At the same time Rabat, Cairo, Algiers and Tunis tighten their own borders, so the region gets easier to route through and harder to sell into.

geopolitics.text: Brussels presented the Pact for the Mediterranean, promising trade, connectivity and investment with its southern neighbours.
Chinese battery investment in Morocco revived European concerns, with Maroš Šefčovič warning about Chinese goods reaching the EU via Morocco.
The Houthis have taken Mocha and moved towards islands near Bab el-Mandeb, and carriers returning to Suez reserve the right to reverse course.
Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri was appointed Morocco's head of government after the 23 September election and must build a coalition.

decision.text: Morocco ended the 1,250-dirham exemption for purchases from international e-commerce platforms, so inbound parcels pay duties and taxes.
Egypt made Advance Cargo Information mandatory for air freight: the importer must obtain an ACID number before shipment.
The EU carbon border mechanism entered its definitive regime for cement, steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen.
Algeria requires a forward import programme approved by the trade ministry, and imports of services now also need authorisation.
Tunisia's central bank requires 100% self-financing for imports of non-essential goods such as clothing and household appliances.
The Commission's maritime ETS review lowers the transshipment share that defines a neighbouring non-EU port from 65% to 50%.

market.text: Tanger Med handled 11.1 million TEU in 2025, up 8.4%.
ETS costs moved relay traffic from Algeciras, whose transshipment fell from 5.2 to 4.6 million TEU, to Tanger Med.
Suez Canal revenue rose 56.7% to $567.1 million in August, but daily transits from January to August averaged 40.8 against 73.7 in 2023.
Nador West Med's East Terminal, operated by Marsa Maroc and MSC's terminal arm, is ready for first commercial calls in the fourth quarter.
Marsa Maroc grew first-half EBITDA 20% on 3% more tonnage, with transshipment down 4%.

parcel.text: Faster restocking: services back on Suez save up to 14 days eastbound, and about four weeks for one Asia to Europe loop compared with the Cape.
More relay at Moroccan hubs means more feeder legs into EU ports and more reliance on ro-ro truck capacity across the Strait of Gibraltar.
Egypt pushes compliance upstream: no air shipment should load without an ACID number, with CargoX platform fees reported at $200 to $300.
Inbound e-commerce parcels into Morocco pay duties such as 40% on clothing plus 20% VAT.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: Moroccan hubs gain from Suez rerouting and EU carbon rules on sea relay and consolidated B2B loads, but the EU's per-parcel charges make direct consumer parcels from Morocco no cheaper than from Asia. Clearing upstream with duties shown at checkout is the condition for selling into Morocco and Egypt, while Algeria and Tunisia stay approval-led B2B markets.

next.text: Morocco: statutory deadline to file the 2027 finance bill, subject to coalition timing
Last of four Gemini services sails via the Red Sea and Suez
EU: first annual CBAM declaration due for 2026 imports

storylines.title: Britain between three rulebooks
storylines.why: Outside the EU, Britain sets its own customs timetable, but it sells into Brussels and Washington on their terms and still courts Beijing. It will close its £135 gap only by October 2028, which leaves the UK as the soft landing for direct parcels while its own exporters face tougher terms in both main markets.

geopolitics.text: The UK-US Economic Prosperity Deal delivered sector access, but its paperless trade and customs work is rated as stalled.
Keir Starmer made the first prime ministerial visit to Beijing in eight years and won a cut in China's whisky tariff.
Andy Burnham became Prime Minister after Starmer's resignation, and the EU-UK summit planned for 22 July was postponed.

decision.text: VAT on consignments of £135 or less is charged at the point of sale, with online marketplaces as deemed suppliers.
The Treasury confirmed removal of the £135 relief by October 2028, with full tariff classification, a per-consignment handling fee and UK fiscal representatives with joint liability.
British goods pay a 10% Section 301 tariff on top of normal duties in the United States, while the EU's combined rate is capped.
British web shops selling into the EU pay the €3 duty per tariff line and, from 1 November, the €2 handling fee per item.

market.text: Ofcom recorded a 19.8% rise in inbound international parcels in 2024-25, mainly from China.
Shein opened its automated centre at Cannock as platforms move part of their UK stock onshore.
Bloomberg analysis put UK low-value imports from December to April at about $1.8 billion, more than France and Germany combined but 11% lower than a year earlier.
Evri passed 1 billion parcels a year after merging with DHL eCommerce UK.

parcel.text: Fewer direct parcels overall, but a larger share of Europe's remaining direct flow lands in Britain until 2028.
From 2028 direct parcels carry full classification, a handling fee per consignment and the cost of a fiscal representative.
Non-UK sellers and marketplaces must appoint UK fiscal representatives with joint and several liability for customs debts.
Bulk imports into UK warehouses shift the fight to domestic last mile and locker density rather than international gateways.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: the timing of the closure, not the principle, decides who gains, and every month of delay keeps the UK the last large Western market where the direct model works on its original economics. British exporters face the worst of both borders, which pushes EU-bound and US-bound stock into the EU or third countries and away from UK outbound gateways.

next.text: Autumn Budget: watch the low-value import timetable and handling fee
EU €2 handling fee per item applies to British online sellers too
Latest date for removal of the £135 low-value import relief (October 2028)

storylines.title: Networks consolidate
storylines.why: Letter decline, labour costs and the shrinking direct cross-border flow are squeezing parcel margins, so density in out-of-home delivery and pricing power now matter more than raw volume. Capital is consolidating networks: lockers, takeovers and the posts' pivot from mail to parcels, under governments that still guard the universal service.

geopolitics.text: PostEurop warned that the EU customs reform puts the cross-border postal universal service at risk.
Britain's new Prime Minister is described as favouring more regulation, as Royal Mail misses letter targets while chasing parcel growth.

decision.text: The UK government cleared EP Group's takeover of Royal Mail with undertakings on headquarters, tax residency and the universal service, backed by a golden share.
Ofcom allowed Second Class letters on alternate weekdays, freeing resources the regulator says can go to parcels.
Denmark's national mail service ended, leaving PostNord Denmark with an operating loss in the transition.
Swiss Post agreed price adjustments with its price regulator from 2027.

market.text: Evri merged with DHL eCommerce UK and passed 1 billion parcels a year.
Royal Mail's out-of-home volumes rose 40%, and GLS's out-of-home network passed 110,000 points.
La Poste's Geopost parcels grew 7.9% while mail fell 11.8%, and the group booked a €182 million impairment on cross-border e-commerce assets.
Bnode cut its 2026 guidance after a strike and a 9.2% fall in parcels.
A consortium led by Advent and FedEx secured 89.8% of InPost in its takeover offer, with delisting to follow.

parcel.text: Lockers become the strategic asset: InPost's network grew 29% to 68,925 machines.
Domestic delivery prices are under pressure, with UK parcel revenue down 0.8% in real terms as volumes rose 7.1%, while FedEx lifts 2027 list rates by 5.9%.
Posts still grow domestic parcels, such as Poste Italiane at 11%, while international flows fall, about 15% at PostNL.
Service quality is slipping in places: Royal Mail's First Class hit 75.7% on time against a 93% target, prompting an Ofcom investigation.

storylines.our_read: Our reading: lockers and out-of-home density are now the strategic asset, as FedEx's move on InPost shows, and the winners will combine density with pricing power rather than raw volume. Posts that lose letters faster than they gain parcels will lean on state support, asset sales or partnerships, so we expect more consolidation in 2027.
